# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Route polyline showing completed vs upcoming trail segments
  - Day markers with tooltips displaying location name and altitude
  - Fly-to animation when clicking itinerary days (scroll-sync)
  - Altitude indicator below map showing current day stats
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons
- `ItineraryAccordion` now supports `onDayChange` callback and active day highlighting

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Changed
- Complete homepage redesign for a more distinctive, less generic look
- Hero: split layout with floating image cards, gradient text, trust indicators, wave SVG transition
- Activities: bento grid with real photography and hover-reveal descriptions
- Featured treks: cards with glassmorphism price badges
- Testimonials: dark section with glassmorphism cards and glow effects on hover
- CTA: full-bleed background image with dual action buttons

### Added
- 28 real images sourced from Unsplash served locally (`public/images/`)
  - Trek hero images for all 6 treks
  - Activity category photos (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding, rafting, skiing, city tours)
  - Gallery page photos
  - Hero banner, sidebar, and CTA background images
- Gallery page with masonry layout and lightbox (prev/next navigation, keyboard-friendly)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect
- Language switcher in header (swaps `/en/...` <-> `/zh/...`)
- Nepal-inspired color theme: forest green, earth tone, adventure orange
- **Pages**: Home, About, Treks (listing + 6 detail pages), Team, Gallery, Contact
- **6 fully detailed treks** with bilingual content:
  - Everest Base Camp (14 days, challenging, $1,800)
  - Annapurna Circuit (18 days, challenging, $1,600)
  - Langtang Valley (10 days, moderate, $900)
  - Manaslu Circuit (16 days, strenuous, $2,200)
  - Poon Hill (5 days, easy, $500)
  - Upper Mustang (14 days, moderate, $2,500)
- Day-by-day itineraries with expandable accordion UI for each trek
- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

message.content: hmm i need ideas on improving the UX, maybe keep map zoomed out and then the day in view and the route for that day is highlighted on the map. what are your thoughts

content.text:
Good idea. Here's what I think would work well:

**Keep the map zoomed out** showing the full route at all times, rather than flying in to each waypoint. This gives users the big-picture context of where they are on the trek.

**Highlight the active day's segment** - the route up to the current day is solid/bright, the rest is faded/dashed. The active day's marker pulses or is larger. This way the user always sees progress along the full route.

A few more thoughts:

- **Smooth polyline progression** instead of abrupt changes - as each day scrolls into view, the "completed" portion of the route extends to that waypoint with a transition
- **Subtle zoom adjustment** - not a full fly-to, but maybe a slight re-center if the active waypoint is near the edge of the viewport, keeping the full route visible
- **Active marker popup** - permanently show a tooltip on the active day's marker with the name/altitude, dismiss others to keep it clean
- **Altitude profile** - a small elevation chart below the map showing the trek profile with a vertical line indicating the current day position. This is more useful than just a number

Want me to go ahead and implement this approach? To summarize:

1. Map stays zoomed to fit full route bounds (no fly-to)
2. Route progressively highlights as you scroll (completed = solid accent, upcoming = faded dashed)
3. Active day marker is enlarged with a permanent tooltip
4. Small altitude profile sparkline below the map showing current position

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Route polyline showing completed vs upcoming trail segments
  - Day markers with tooltips displaying location name and altitude
  - Fly-to animation when clicking itinerary days (scroll-sync)
  - Altitude indicator below map showing current day stats
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons
- `ItineraryAccordion` now supports `onDayChange` callback and active day highlighting

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Changed
- Complete homepage redesign for a more distinctive, less generic look
- Hero: split layout with floating image cards, gradient text, trust indicators, wave SVG transition
- Activities: bento grid with real photography and hover-reveal descriptions
- Featured treks: cards with glassmorphism price badges
- Testimonials: dark section with glassmorphism cards and glow effects on hover
- CTA: full-bleed background image with dual action buttons

### Added
- 28 real images sourced from Unsplash served locally (`public/images/`)
  - Trek hero images for all 6 treks
  - Activity category photos (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding, rafting, skiing, city tours)
  - Gallery page photos
  - Hero banner, sidebar, and CTA background images
- Gallery page with masonry layout and lightbox (prev/next navigation, keyboard-friendly)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect
- Language switcher in header (swaps `/en/...` <-> `/zh/...`)
- Nepal-inspired color theme: forest green, earth tone, adventure orange
- **Pages**: Home, About, Treks (listing + 6 detail pages), Team, Gallery, Contact
- **6 fully detailed treks** with bilingual content:
  - Everest Base Camp (14 days, challenging, $1,800)
  - Annapurna Circuit (18 days, challenging, $1,600)
  - Langtang Valley (10 days, moderate, $900)
  - Manaslu Circuit (16 days, strenuous, $2,200)
  - Poon Hill (5 days, easy, $500)
  - Upper Mustang (14 days, moderate, $2,500)
- Day-by-day itineraries with expandable accordion UI for each trek
- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

Build passes. Here's a summary of the two bugs fixed:

**Bug 1 — `activeDay` truthiness** (`TrekMap.tsx:82`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx:28`): Used `activeDay ?` which treats `null` as falsy and falls back to index `0`, so day 1 was always marked as completed/active regardless. Fixed to `activeDay !== null ? ... : -1`.

**Bug 2 — IntersectionObserver reporting** (`ItineraryAccordion.tsx:24`): The observer callback only receives entries whose intersection *changed*, not all visible elements. So the "pick the best" logic was choosing from a partial set, causing the active day to flicker or jump. Fixed by maintaining a persistent `visibleMap` ref that tracks all currently visible entries and their ratios, then picking the best from the full set on every callback. Also added more threshold steps (`[0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1]`) for smoother updates.

CHANGELOG has been updated with all the map UX changes, the new altitude profile, and these two fixes.

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Itinerary days are now always expanded (no collapsible accordion) for easier scrolling
- Scroll-driven map sync via IntersectionObserver — the map advances as the user scrolls through days
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

### Fixed
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback
- IntersectionObserver only reported *changed* entries, causing active day to flicker; now tracks all visible entries persistently and picks the most visible

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Changed
- Complete homepage redesign for a more distinctive, less generic look
- Hero: split layout with floating image cards, gradient text, trust indicators, wave SVG transition
- Activities: bento grid with real photography and hover-reveal descriptions
- Featured treks: cards with glassmorphism price badges
- Testimonials: dark section with glassmorphism cards and glow effects on hover
- CTA: full-bleed background image with dual action buttons

### Added
- 28 real images sourced from Unsplash served locally (`public/images/`)
  - Trek hero images for all 6 treks
  - Activity category photos (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding, rafting, skiing, city tours)
  - Gallery page photos
  - Hero banner, sidebar, and CTA background images
- Gallery page with masonry layout and lightbox (prev/next navigation, keyboard-friendly)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect
- Language switcher in header (swaps `/en/...` <-> `/zh/...`)
- Nepal-inspired color theme: forest green, earth tone, adventure orange
- **Pages**: Home, About, Treks (listing + 6 detail pages), Team, Gallery, Contact
- **6 fully detailed treks** with bilingual content:
  - Everest Base Camp (14 days, challenging, $1,800)
  - Annapurna Circuit (18 days, challenging, $1,600)
  - Langtang Valley (10 days, moderate, $900)
  - Manaslu Circuit (16 days, strenuous, $2,200)
  - Poon Hill (5 days, easy, $500)
  - Upper Mustang (14 days, moderate, $2,500)
- Day-by-day itineraries with expandable accordion UI for each trek
- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

content.text:
Build passes. Two fixes:

**Tooltip bug**: The `CircleMarker` key was `${wp.day}-${wp.lat}-${wp.lng}` which is stable, so react-leaflet never remounted the `Tooltip` when `permanent` toggled between `true`/`false`. Leaflet bakes the `permanent` state at creation time. Fixed by adding `isActive` to the key (`${wp.day}-${wp.lat}-${wp.lng}-${isActive}`), forcing the marker + tooltip to remount when active state changes.

**Header gap**: Set the main header to an explicit `h-16` (64px) instead of relying on padding, then matched the sticky trek header with `top-16`. No more pixel guessing or gap.

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero
  - Shows trek name, difficulty dot, duration, altitude, price, and Book CTA
  - Frosted glass dark background with slide-in/out animation
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- Replaced all 6 trek hero images with higher-quality, trek-specific Unsplash photos
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Itinerary days are now always expanded (no collapsible accordion) for easier scrolling
- Scroll-driven map sync via IntersectionObserver — the map advances as the user scrolls through days
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

### Fixed
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback
- IntersectionObserver only reported *changed* entries, causing active day to flicker; now tracks all visible entries persistently and picks the most visible
- Last itinerary days unreachable by scroll observer; added bottom padding (`pb-[40vh]`) so final days can scroll into the observation zone

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero
  - Shows trek name, difficulty dot, duration, altitude, price, and Book CTA
  - Frosted glass dark background with slide-in/out animation
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed

# CLAUDE.md

## Project Overview

**Find Nepal Trek** — a bilingual (English + Traditional Chinese) trekking company website built with Next.js, statically exported for deployment.

## Tech Stack

- **Framework**: Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- **Language**: TypeScript (strict mode)
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4
- **React**: v19
- **Maps**: Leaflet + react-leaflet (loaded via `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`)
- **Fonts**: Inter (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts

## Key Architecture Decisions

- **Static export**: `output: "export"` in `next.config.ts` — no server-side features (no API routes, no SSR, no middleware). All pages are pre-rendered at build time.
- **i18n**: `[lang]` dynamic route segments with `generateStaticParams()` producing `/en/*` and `/zh/*` routes. Dictionary JSON files at `src/dictionaries/en.json` and `zh.json`.
- **Images**: `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility. All images served from `public/images/`.
- **No SSR for Leaflet**: Leaflet requires `window` — always use `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`, never `React.lazy()`.

## Color Theme

- Primary (forest green): `#1B4332`
- Secondary (earth tone): `#D4A373`
- Accent (adventure orange): `#E76F51`

## Project Structure

```
src/
├── app/[lang]/          # All pages under language segment
├── components/          # React components (layout, home, treks, etc.)
├── data/                # Trek data, team data, GPS coordinates
├── dictionaries/        # en.json, zh.json translation files
└── types/               # TypeScript interfaces
```

## Commands

- `npm run dev` — Start dev server
- `npm run build` — Production build (outputs to `out/`)
- `npx serve out` — Serve the static build locally

## Workflow Rules

- **All changes must be documented in CHANGELOG.md** following the existing format (Keep a Changelog style with Added/Changed/Fixed sections).
- **All changes must be committed with descriptive messages and pushed** — commit messages should summarize the "why", not just the "what".
- When adding bilingual content, always update both English and Chinese versions.
- Prefer editing existing files over creating new ones.

# CLAUDE.md

## Project Overview

**Find Nepal Trek** — a bilingual (English + Traditional Chinese) trekking company website built with Next.js, statically exported for deployment.

## Tech Stack

- **Framework**: Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- **Language**: TypeScript (strict mode)
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4
- **React**: v19
- **Maps**: Leaflet + react-leaflet (loaded via `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`)
- **Fonts**: Inter (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts

## Key Architecture Decisions

- **Static export**: `output: "export"` in `next.config.ts` — no server-side features (no API routes, no SSR, no middleware). All pages are pre-rendered at build time.
- **i18n**: `[lang]` dynamic route segments with `generateStaticParams()` producing `/en/*` and `/zh/*` routes. Dictionary JSON files at `src/dictionaries/en.json` and `zh.json`.
- **Images**: `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility. All images served from `public/images/`.
- **No SSR for Leaflet**: Leaflet requires `window` — always use `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`, never `React.lazy()`.

## Color Theme

- Primary (forest green): `#1B4332`
- Secondary (earth tone): `#D4A373`
- Accent (adventure orange): `#E76F51`

## Project Structure

```
src/
├── app/[lang]/          # All pages under language segment
├── components/          # React components (layout, home, treks, etc.)
├── data/                # Trek data, team data, GPS coordinates
├── dictionaries/        # en.json, zh.json translation files
└── types/               # TypeScript interfaces
```

## Commands

- `npm run dev` — Start dev server
- `npm run build` — Production build (outputs to `out/`)
- `npx serve out` — Serve the static build locally

## Workflow Rules

- **All changes must be documented in CHANGELOG.md** following the existing format (Keep a Changelog style with Added/Changed/Fixed sections).
- **All changes must be committed with descriptive messages and pushed** — commit messages should summarize the "why", not just the "what".
- When adding bilingual content, always update both English and Chinese versions.
- Prefer editing existing files over creating new ones.

import type { TeamMember } from "@/types/trek";

export const team: TeamMember[] = [
  {
    id: "ram",
    nameEn: "Ram Gurung",
    nameZh: "拉姆·古隆",
    roleEn: "Founder & Lead Guide",
    roleZh: "創辦人暨首席嚮導",
    bioEn:
      "Born and raised in the foothills of the Annapurna range, Ram has over 15 years of professional trekking and mountaineering experience. He holds international mountain guide certifications and is trained in high-altitude medicine. His deep knowledge of Nepal's trails, culture, and people makes every trek an authentic and safe adventure.",
    bioZh:
      "在安納普爾納山麓出生長大的拉姆，擁有超過 15 年的專業登山與健行經驗。他持有國際登山嚮導認證，並受過高海拔醫學訓練。對尼泊爾步道、文化和人民的深入了解，讓每一趟行程都成為真實且安全的冒險體驗。",
    image: "/images/team/ram.jpg",
    languages: ["Nepali", "English", "Chinese", "Hindi"],
  },
  {
    id: "mei",
    nameEn: "Mei-Ling Chen",
    nameZh: "陳美玲",
    roleEn: "Co-Founder & Trip Planner",
    roleZh: "共同創辦人暨行程規劃師",
    bioEn:
      "Originally from Taiwan, Mei-Ling fell in love with Nepal during her first visit and never looked back. She brings meticulous planning skills and a warm understanding of what Chinese-speaking travelers need to feel at home abroad. She handles all itinerary design, client communications, and ensures every detail is perfectly arranged.",
    bioZh:
      "來自台灣的美玲，第一次造訪尼泊爾就深深愛上了這片土地。她帶來細心的行程規劃能力，深刻理解華語旅客在海外旅行時的需求。她負責所有行程設計、客戶溝通，確保每個細節都安排得完美無瑕。",
    image: "/images/team/mei.jpg",
    languages: ["Chinese", "English", "Nepali"],
  },
  {
    id: "pasang",
    nameEn: "Pasang Sherpa",
    nameZh: "帕桑·雪巴",
    roleEn: "Senior Trekking Guide",
    roleZh: "資深登山嚮導",
    bioEn:
      "A native of the Khumbu region, Pasang has summited several peaks above 6,000 meters and has guided hundreds of trekkers to Everest Base Camp. His calm demeanor, encyclopedic knowledge of Sherpa culture, and unwavering attention to safety make him one of the most trusted guides in Nepal.",
    bioZh:
      "帕桑是昆布地區的原住民，曾攀登多座六千公尺以上的山峰，帶領數百位旅客成功抵達聖母峰基地營。他沉穩的性格、對雪巴文化的百科全書式知識，以及對安全的堅定關注，讓他成為尼泊爾最受信賴的嚮導之一。",
    image: "/images/team/pasang.jpg",
    languages: ["Nepali", "English", "Sherpa"],
  },
  {
    id: "dawa",
    nameEn: "Dawa Tamang",
    nameZh: "達瓦·塔芒",
    roleEn: "Trekking Guide & Photographer",
    roleZh: "登山嚮導暨攝影師",
    bioEn:
      "Dawa combines his passion for the outdoors with a talent for photography, capturing the stunning landscapes and candid moments that make each trek special. He specializes in the Langtang and Manaslu regions and loves sharing stories of local traditions with travelers.",
    bioZh:
      "達瓦將他對戶外的熱情與攝影才華完美結合，捕捉壯麗的風景和真實的瞬間，讓每趟行程都格外特別。他專精於藍塘和馬納斯盧地區，喜歡與旅客分享當地傳統的故事。",
    image: "/images/team/dawa.jpg",
    languages: ["Nepali", "English", "Tamang"],
  },
];

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero
  - Shows trek name, difficulty dot, duration, altitude, price, and Book CTA
  - Frosted glass dark background with slide-in/out animation
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- Replaced all 6 trek hero images with higher-quality, trek-specific Unsplash photos
- Main header set to explicit `h-16` for consistent layout
- Disabled elastic/rubber-band overscroll globally (`overscroll-behavior: none`)
- **Contact page redesigned**: removed form, replaced with phone/WhatsApp card, email card with pre-filled mailto template, numbered checklist of what to include, and info cards (location, response time, languages)
- Removed Contact from header and footer navigation (still reachable via booking CTAs throughout the site)
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Itinerary days are now always expanded (no collapsible accordion) for easier scrolling
- Scroll-driven map sync via IntersectionObserver — the map advances as the user scrolls through days
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

### Fixed
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback
- IntersectionObserver only reported *changed* entries, causing active day to flicker; now tracks all visible entries persistently and picks the most visible
- Last itinerary days unreachable by scroll observer; added bottom padding (`pb-[40vh]`) so final days can scroll into the observation zone
- Map tooltips not updating when active day changes; Leaflet `Tooltip` with `permanent` prop is baked at creation time, so added `isActive` to the `CircleMarker` key to force remount
- Gap between main header and sticky trek header; set header to explicit `h-16` and matched with `top-16`

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Changed
- Complete homepage redesign for a more distinctive, less generic look
- Hero: split layout with floating image cards, gradient text, trust indicators, wave SVG transition
- Activities: bento grid with real photography and hover-reveal descriptions
- Featured treks: cards with glassmorphism price badges
- Testimonials: dark section with glassmorphism cards and glow effects on hover
- CTA: full-bleed background image with dual action buttons

### Added
- 28 real images sourced from Unsplash served locally (`public/images/`)
  - Trek hero images for all 6 treks
  - Activity category photos (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding, rafting, skiing, city tours)
  - Gallery page photos
  - Hero banner, sidebar, and CTA background images
- Gallery page with masonry layout and lightbox (prev/next navigation, keyboard-friendly)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect
- Language switcher in header (swaps `/en/...` <-> `/zh/...`)
- Nepal-inspired color theme: forest green, earth tone, adventure orange
- **Pages**: Home, About, Treks (listing + 6 detail pages), Team, Gallery, Contact
- **6 fully detailed treks** with bilingual content:
  - Everest Base Camp (14 days, challenging, $1,800)
  - Annapurna Circuit (18 days, challenging, $1,600)
  - Langtang Valley (10 days, moderate, $900)
  - Manaslu Circuit (16 days, strenuous, $2,200)
  - Poon Hill (5 days, easy, $500)
  - Upper Mustang (14 days, moderate, $2,500)
- Day-by-day itineraries with expandable accordion UI for each trek
- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero
  - Shows trek name, difficulty dot, duration, altitude, price, and Book CTA
  - Frosted glass dark background with slide-in/out animation
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- **About page content updated** to match original WordPress site copy
  - Hero title changed to "About Us" / "關於我們"
  - Story section uses authentic bilingual copy: "台灣女婿" / "台灣女兒" phrasing
  - All 6 principle titles and descriptions updated to match WordPress originals (more literary/poetic tone)
  - English translations rewritten to faithfully reflect the Chinese source
- **Team page updated**: reduced to 3 members (Shiva, Mei-Ling, Rainbow), added real team photo, page now shows actual images when available with initial-letter fallback, gracefully handles empty fields
- Replaced all 6 trek hero images with higher-quality, trek-specific Unsplash photos
- Main header set to explicit `h-16` for consistent layout
- Disabled elastic/rubber-band overscroll globally (`overscroll-behavior: none`)
- **Contact page redesigned**: removed form, replaced with phone/WhatsApp card, email card with pre-filled mailto template, numbered checklist of what to include, and info cards (location, response time, languages)
- Removed Contact from header and footer navigation (still reachable via booking CTAs throughout the site)
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Itinerary days are now always expanded (no collapsible accordion) for easier scrolling
- Scroll-driven map sync via IntersectionObserver — the map advances as the user scrolls through days
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

### Fixed
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback
- IntersectionObserver only reported *changed* entries, causing active day to flicker; now tracks all visible entries persistently and picks the most visible
- Last itinerary days unreachable by scroll observer; added bottom padding (`pb-[40vh]`) so final days can scroll into the observation zone

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero
  - Shows trek name, difficulty dot, duration, altitude, price, and Book CTA
  - Frosted glass dark background with slide-in/out animation
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- **About page content updated** to match original WordPress site copy
  - Hero title changed to "About Us" / "關於我們"
  - Story section uses authentic bilingual copy: "台灣女婿" / "台灣女兒" phrasing
  - All 6 principle titles and descriptions updated to match WordPress originals (more literary/poetic tone)
  - English translations rewritten to faithfully reflect the Chinese source
- **Team page updated**: reduced to 3 members (Shiva, Mei-Ling, Rainbow), added real team photo, page now shows actual images when available with initial-letter fallback, gracefully handles empty fields
- Replaced all 6 trek hero images with higher-quality, trek-specific Unsplash photos
- Main header set to explicit `h-16` for consistent layout
- Disabled elastic/rubber-band overscroll globally (`overscroll-behavior: none`)
- **Contact page redesigned**: removed form, replaced with phone/WhatsApp card, email card with pre-filled mailto template, numbered checklist of what to include, and info cards (location, response time, languages)
- Removed Contact from header and footer navigation (still reachable via booking CTAs throughout the site)
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Itinerary days are now always expanded (no collapsible accordion) for easier scrolling
- Scroll-driven map sync via IntersectionObserver — the map advances as the user scrolls through days
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

### Fixed
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback
- IntersectionObserver only reported *changed* entries, causing active day to flicker; now tracks all visible entries persistently and picks the most visible
- Last itinerary days unreachable by scroll observer; added bottom padding (`pb-[40vh]`) so final days can scroll into the observation zone
- Map tooltips not updating when active day changes; Leaflet `Tooltip` with `permanent` prop is baked at creation time, so added `isActive` to the `CircleMarker` key to force remount
- Gap between main header and sticky trek header; set header to explicit `h-16` and matched with `top-16`

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Changed
- Complete homepage redesign for a more distinctive, less generic look
- Hero: split layout with floating image cards, gradient text, trust indicators, wave SVG transition
- Activities: bento grid with real photography and hover-reveal descriptions
- Featured treks: cards with glassmorphism price badges
- Testimonials: dark section with glassmorphism cards and glow effects on hover
- CTA: full-bleed background image with dual action buttons

### Added
- 28 real images sourced from Unsplash served locally (`public/images/`)
  - Trek hero images for all 6 treks
  - Activity category photos (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding, rafting, skiing, city tours)
  - Gallery page photos
  - Hero banner, sidebar, and CTA background images
- Gallery page with masonry layout and lightbox (prev/next navigation, keyboard-friendly)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect
- Language switcher in header (swaps `/en/...` <-> `/zh/...`)
- Nepal-inspired color theme: forest green, earth tone, adventure orange
- **Pages**: Home, About, Treks (listing + 6 detail pages), Team, Gallery, Contact
- **6 fully detailed treks** with bilingual content:
  - Everest Base Camp (14 days, challenging, $1,800)
  - Annapurna Circuit (18 days, challenging, $1,600)
  - Langtang Valley (10 days, moderate, $900)
  - Manaslu Circuit (16 days, strenuous, $2,200)
  - Poon Hill (5 days, easy, $500)
  - Upper Mustang (14 days, moderate, $2,500)
- Day-by-day itineraries with expandable accordion UI for each trek
- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

content.text:
The scroll-sync map is really a desktop experience — the sticky sidebar layout, IntersectionObserver triggering, and Leaflet interactions don't translate well to narrow screens. A few options:

1. **Hide map on mobile, show itinerary only** — cleanest, zero compromise. Could keep the altitude profile since it's just a small SVG.
2. **Non-sticky map at the top** — show the map once before the itinerary, no scroll sync. Simpler but adds a big static block.
3. **Collapsible "View Map" button** — toggle the map open/closed. More code, somewhat clunky UX.

I'd recommend option 1 — hide the map column on mobile with a `hidden lg:block` and let the itinerary take full width. Want me to go with that?

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero
  - Shows trek name, difficulty dot, duration, altitude, price, and Book CTA
  - Frosted glass dark background with slide-in/out animation
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- **About page content updated** to match original WordPress site copy
  - Hero title changed to "About Us" / "關於我們"
  - Story section uses authentic bilingual copy: "台灣女婿" / "台灣女兒" phrasing
  - All 6 principle titles and descriptions updated to match WordPress originals (more literary/poetic tone)
  - English translations rewritten to faithfully reflect the Chinese source
- **Team page updated**: 3 members (Shiva, guide2, Rainbow) with real photos where available
  - Vertical card layout with fixed-height cover images, uniform card sizing
  - 3-column grid on desktop; gracefully handles empty name/role/bio/languages
- **About page principle cards redesigned**: removed generic Heroicon bubbles, replaced with numbered editorial layout (left accent border, large decorative `01`–`06` watermark numbers, rounded cards with shadow)
- Stats section (years experience, happy trekkers, etc.) commented out until real numbers confirmed
- Replaced all 6 trek hero images with higher-quality, trek-specific Unsplash photos
- Main header set to explicit `h-16` for consistent layout
- Disabled elastic/rubber-band overscroll globally (`overscroll-behavior: none`)
- **Contact page redesigned**: removed form, replaced with phone/WhatsApp card, email card with pre-filled mailto template, numbered checklist of what to include, and info cards (location, response time, languages)
- Removed Contact from header and footer navigation (still reachable via booking CTAs throughout the site)
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Itinerary days are now always expanded (no collapsible accordion) for easier scrolling
- Scroll-driven map sync via IntersectionObserver — the map advances as the user scrolls through days
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

### Fixed
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback
- IntersectionObserver only reported *changed* entries, causing active day to flicker; now tracks all visible entries persistently and picks the most visible
- Last itinerary days unreachable by scroll observer; added bottom padding (`pb-[40vh]`) so final days can scroll into the observation zone
- Map tooltips not updating when active day changes; Leaflet `Tooltip` with `permanent` prop is baked at creation time, so added `isActive` to the `CircleMarker` key to force remount
- Gap between main header and sticky trek header; set header to explicit `h-16` and matched with `top-16`

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Changed
- Complete homepage redesign for a more distinctive, less generic look
- Hero: split layout with floating image cards, gradient text, trust indicators, wave SVG transition
- Activities: bento grid with real photography and hover-reveal descriptions
- Featured treks: cards with glassmorphism price badges
- Testimonials: dark section with glassmorphism cards and glow effects on hover
- CTA: full-bleed background image with dual action buttons

### Added
- 28 real images sourced from Unsplash served locally (`public/images/`)
  - Trek hero images for all 6 treks
  - Activity category photos (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding, rafting, skiing, city tours)
  - Gallery page photos
  - Hero banner, sidebar, and CTA background images
- Gallery page with masonry layout and lightbox (prev/next navigation, keyboard-friendly)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect
- Language switcher in header (swaps `/en/...` <-> `/zh/...`)
- Nepal-inspired color theme: forest green, earth tone, adventure orange
- **Pages**: Home, About, Treks (listing + 6 detail pages), Team, Gallery, Contact
- **6 fully detailed treks** with bilingual content:
  - Everest Base Camp (14 days, challenging, $1,800)
  - Annapurna Circuit (18 days, challenging, $1,600)
  - Langtang Valley (10 days, moderate, $900)
  - Manaslu Circuit (16 days, strenuous, $2,200)
  - Poon Hill (5 days, easy, $500)
  - Upper Mustang (14 days, moderate, $2,500)
- Day-by-day itineraries with expandable accordion UI for each trek
- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero
  - Shows trek name, difficulty dot, duration, altitude, price, and Book CTA
  - Frosted glass dark background with slide-in/out animation
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- **About page content updated** to match original WordPress site copy
  - Hero title changed to "About Us" / "關於我們"
  - Story section uses authentic bilingual copy: "台灣女婿" / "台灣女兒" phrasing
  - All 6 principle titles and descriptions updated to match WordPress originals (more literary/poetic tone)
  - English translations rewritten to faithfully reflect the Chinese source
- **Team page updated**: 3 members (Shiva, guide2, Rainbow) with real photos where available
  - Vertical card layout with fixed-height cover images, uniform card sizing
  - 3-column grid on desktop; gracefully handles empty name/role/bio/languages
- **About page principle cards redesigned**: removed generic Heroicon bubbles, replaced with numbered editorial layout (left accent border, large decorative `01`–`06` watermark numbers, rounded cards with shadow)
- Stats section (years experience, happy trekkers, etc.) commented out until real numbers confirmed
- Replaced all 6 trek hero images with higher-quality, trek-specific Unsplash photos
- Main header set to explicit `h-16` for consistent layout
- Disabled elastic/rubber-band overscroll globally (`overscroll-behavior: none`)
- **Contact page redesigned**: removed form, replaced with phone/WhatsApp card, email card with pre-filled mailto template, numbered checklist of what to include, and info cards (location, response time, languages)
- Removed Contact from header and footer navigation (still reachable via booking CTAs throughout the site)
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Itinerary days are now always expanded (no collapsible accordion) for easier scrolling
- Scroll-driven map sync via IntersectionObserver — the map advances as the user scrolls through days
- **Mobile trek map**: non-sticky map + altitude profile shown at top on mobile; sticky sidebar layout on desktop only
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

### Fixed
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback
- IntersectionObserver only reported *changed* entries, causing active day to flicker; now tracks all visible entries persistently and picks the most visible
- Last itinerary days unreachable by scroll observer; added bottom padding (`pb-[40vh]`) so final days can scroll into the observation zone
- Map tooltips not updating when active day changes; Leaflet `Tooltip` with `permanent` prop is baked at creation time, so added `isActive` to the `CircleMarker` key to force remount
- Gap between main header and sticky trek header; set header to explicit `h-16` and matched with `top-16`

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Changed
- Complete homepage redesign for a more distinctive, less generic look
- Hero: split layout with floating image cards, gradient text, trust indicators, wave SVG transition
- Activities: bento grid with real photography and hover-reveal descriptions
- Featured treks: cards with glassmorphism price badges
- Testimonials: dark section with glassmorphism cards and glow effects on hover
- CTA: full-bleed background image with dual action buttons

### Added
- 28 real images sourced from Unsplash served locally (`public/images/`)
  - Trek hero images for all 6 treks
  - Activity category photos (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding, rafting, skiing, city tours)
  - Gallery page photos
  - Hero banner, sidebar, and CTA background images
- Gallery page with masonry layout and lightbox (prev/next navigation, keyboard-friendly)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect
- Language switcher in header (swaps `/en/...` <-> `/zh/...`)
- Nepal-inspired color theme: forest green, earth tone, adventure orange
- **Pages**: Home, About, Treks (listing + 6 detail pages), Team, Gallery, Contact
- **6 fully detailed treks** with bilingual content:
  - Everest Base Camp (14 days, challenging, $1,800)
  - Annapurna Circuit (18 days, challenging, $1,600)
  - Langtang Valley (10 days, moderate, $900)
  - Manaslu Circuit (16 days, strenuous, $2,200)
  - Poon Hill (5 days, easy, $500)
  - Upper Mustang (14 days, moderate, $2,500)
- Day-by-day itineraries with expandable accordion UI for each trek
- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

lines: - Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

+- **Map z-index overlapping headers**: Leaflet's internal z-index values caused the map to render above the sticky main header (z-50) and trek header (z-40); added `relative z-0` stacking context isolation to the map wrapper
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback

content.content:
# Hero Section Analysis

## Layout & Content

The hero section features a full-width banner image with overlaid text. The primary heading states "歡迎來到 【發現尼伯爾】" (Welcome to Find Nepal Trek), followed by the tagline "我們是提供您 難忘冒險 和 無與倫比旅遊 的專家" (We provide expert guidance for unforgettable adventures and unmatched travel).

## Distinctive Elements

**Bilingual Positioning**: The site prominently displays both Traditional Chinese and English throughout, reflecting its target audience of Chinese-speaking travelers seeking Nepal experiences.

**Navigation Structure**: A dual-language menu system allows seamless switching between Chinese and English versions, with parallel navigation paths.

**Contact Integration**: The phone number "(977) 984 929 2486" is prominently displayed in the header, emphasizing direct accessibility alongside the bilingual capability statement: "我們 中文 英文 都通喔!" (We speak English and Chinese!).

**Visual Approach**: Rather than generic stock imagery, the banner uses scenic photography of Nepal landscapes, immediately establishing the adventure tourism context and differentiating from template-heavy competitors.

**Service Categories**: Below the hero, the page immediately showcases activity types (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding) through a grid layout, providing clear service differentiation.

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import math

def draw_favicon(size):
    img = Image.new('RGBA', (size, size), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    
    s = size / 32  # scale factor
    
    # Sun
    cx, cy, r = 16*s, 11*s, 5*s
    draw.ellipse([cx-r, cy-r, cx+r, cy+r], fill=(240, 128, 32, 255))
    
    # Left mountain
    draw.polygon([(2*s, 28*s), (10*s, 10*s), (18*s, 28*s)], fill=(30, 18, 10, 255))
    
    # Right mountain
    draw.polygon([(14*s, 28*s), (22*s, 8*s), (30*s, 28*s)], fill=(61, 37, 16, 255))
    
    # Snow caps
    draw.polygon([(10*s, 10*s), (8*s, 14*s), (12*s, 14*s)], fill=(255, 255, 255, 160))
    draw.polygon([(22*s, 8*s), (20*s, 12*s), (24*s, 12*s)], fill=(255, 255, 255, 160))
    
    return img

# Generate various sizes
sizes = {
    'favicon-16x16.png': 16,
    'favicon-32x32.png': 32,
    'apple-icon.png': 180,
}

for filename, size in sizes.items():
    img = draw_favicon(size)
    path = f'/Users/chiu.fyi/work/find-nepal-trek-website/src/app/{filename}'
    img.save(path)
    print(f'Created {filename} ({size}x{size})')

# Also create a favicon.ico with multiple sizes
ico_16 = draw_favicon(16)
ico_32 = draw_favicon(32)
ico_path = '/Users/chiu.fyi/work/find-nepal-trek-website/src/app/favicon.ico'
ico_16.save(ico_path, format='ICO', sizes=[(16, 16), (32, 32)], append_images=[ico_32])
print('Created favicon.ico (16+32)')
" 2>&1

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

def draw_favicon(size):
    img = Image.new('RGBA', (size, size), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    s = size / 32  # scale factor

    # Sun (behind mountains)
    cx, cy, r = 16*s, 14*s, 6*s
    draw.ellipse([cx-r, cy-r, cx+r, cy+r], fill=(240, 128, 32, 255))

    # Right mountain (drawn first, behind left) — brown fill with dark outline
    right_pts = [(12*s, 28*s), (21*s, 8*s), (31*s, 28*s)]
    draw.polygon(right_pts, fill=(160, 90, 24, 255), outline=(30, 18, 10, 255))

    # Left mountain — orange fill with dark outline
    left_pts = [(1*s, 28*s), (11*s, 11*s), (21*s, 28*s)]
    draw.polygon(left_pts, fill=(201, 107, 29, 255), outline=(30, 18, 10, 255))

    # Snow caps (white triangles)
    draw.polygon([(11*s, 11*s), (9*s, 15*s), (13*s, 15*s)], fill=(255, 255, 255, 220))
    draw.polygon([(21*s, 8*s), (19*s, 12*s), (23*s, 12*s)], fill=(255, 255, 255, 220))

    return img

# Generate apple icon

img.save('/Users/chiu.fyi/work/find-nepal-trek-website/src/app/apple-icon.png')
print('Created apple-icon.png (180x180)')

ico_32 = draw_favicon(32)
ico_32.save('/Users/chiu.fyi/work/find-nepal-trek-website/src/app/favicon.ico', format='ICO', sizes=[(16, 16), (32, 32)], append_images=[ico_16])

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont, ImageFilter

# Open hero image
img = Image.open("/Users/chiu.fyi/work/find-nepal-trek-website/public/images/hero-bg.jpg")
print(f"Original size: {img.size}")

# Target: 1200x630 (OG standard)
target_w, target_h = 1200, 630
target_ratio = target_w / target_h

# Center-crop to target ratio
w, h = img.size
img_ratio = w / h

if img_ratio > target_ratio:
    # Image is wider - crop sides
    new_w = int(h * target_ratio)
    left = (w - new_w) // 2
    img = img.crop((left, 0, left + new_w, h))
else:
    # Image is taller - crop top/bottom
    new_h = int(w / target_ratio)
    top = (h - new_h) // 2
    img = img.crop((0, top, w, top + new_h))

# Resize to exact target
img = img.resize((target_w, target_h), Image.LANCZOS)

# Add a dark gradient overlay from bottom
overlay = Image.new("RGBA", (target_w, target_h), (0, 0, 0, 0))
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(overlay)

# Bottom gradient (for text readability)
for y in range(target_h // 2, target_h):
    alpha = int(180 * ((y - target_h // 2) / (target_h // 2)))
    draw.rectangle([(0, y), (target_w, y)], fill=(30, 18, 10, alpha))

# Slight overall tint
tint = Image.new("RGBA", (target_w, target_h), (30, 18, 10, 40))
img = img.convert("RGBA")
img = Image.alpha_composite(img, tint)
img = Image.alpha_composite(img, overlay)

# Add text
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# Try to use a bold system font
font_paths = [
    "/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc",
    "/System/Library/Fonts/SFNSDisplay.ttf",
    "/Library/Fonts/Arial Bold.ttf",
    "/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial Bold.ttf",
]

title_font = None
subtitle_font = None
for fp in font_paths:
    try:
        title_font = ImageFont.truetype(fp, 64)
        subtitle_font = ImageFont.truetype(fp, 28)
        break
    except:
        continue

if title_font is None:
    title_font = ImageFont.load_default()
    subtitle_font = ImageFont.load_default()

# Site name
draw.text((60, target_h - 180), "Find Nepal Trek", font=title_font, fill=(255, 255, 255, 240))

# Tagline

# Convert back to RGB and save
img = img.convert("RGB")
img.save("/Users/chiu.fyi/work/find-nepal-trek-website/public/images/og-image.jpg", quality=90)
print(f"OG image saved: {img.size}")

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded
  - Gentle pan only if the active waypoint drifts near the map edge
  - Sticky sidebar layout: itinerary on the left, map on the right
- **Altitude profile sparkline** (`AltitudeProfile.tsx`) below the map
  - SVG elevation chart showing the full trek profile with min/max labels
  - Completed portion fills in orange matching the map progression
  - Vertical dashed line marks the current day, with day name and altitude below
- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero
  - Shows trek name, difficulty dot, duration, altitude, price, and Book CTA
  - Frosted glass dark background with slide-in/out animation
- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- **About page content updated** to match original WordPress site copy
  - Hero title changed to "About Us" / "關於我們"
  - Story section uses authentic bilingual copy: "台灣女婿" / "台灣女兒" phrasing
  - All 6 principle titles and descriptions updated to match WordPress originals (more literary/poetic tone)
  - English translations rewritten to faithfully reflect the Chinese source
- **Team page updated**: 3 members (Shiva, guide2, Rainbow) with real photos where available
  - Vertical card layout with fixed-height cover images, uniform card sizing
  - 3-column grid on desktop; gracefully handles empty name/role/bio/languages
- **About page principle cards redesigned**: removed generic Heroicon bubbles, replaced with numbered editorial layout (left accent border, large decorative `01`–`06` watermark numbers, rounded cards with shadow)
- Stats section (years experience, happy trekkers, etc.) commented out until real numbers confirmed
- Replaced all 6 trek hero images with higher-quality, trek-specific Unsplash photos
- Main header set to explicit `h-16` for consistent layout
- Disabled elastic/rubber-band overscroll globally (`overscroll-behavior: none`)
- **Contact page redesigned**: removed form, replaced with phone/WhatsApp card, email card with pre-filled mailto template, numbered checklist of what to include, and info cards (location, response time, languages)
- Removed Contact from header and footer navigation (still reachable via booking CTAs throughout the site)
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view
- Itinerary days are now always expanded (no collapsible accordion) for easier scrolling
- Scroll-driven map sync via IntersectionObserver — the map advances as the user scrolls through days
- **Mobile trek map**: non-sticky map + altitude profile shown at top on mobile; sticky sidebar layout on desktop only
- Added info bar below hero with duration, altitude, season, price, and booking CTA
- Added bottom CTA section with booking and inquiry buttons

### Fixed
- **Map z-index overlapping headers**: Leaflet's internal z-index values caused the map to render above the sticky main header (z-50) and trek header (z-40); added `relative z-0` stacking context isolation to the map wrapper
- `activeDay` truthiness bug: `activeDay ? ... : 0` treated `null` as index 0, incorrectly marking day 1 as always active; fixed to use `activeDay !== null` with `-1` fallback
- IntersectionObserver only reported *changed* entries, causing active day to flicker; now tracks all visible entries persistently and picks the most visible
- Last itinerary days unreachable by scroll observer; added bottom padding (`pb-[40vh]`) so final days can scroll into the observation zone
- Map tooltips not updating when active day changes; Leaflet `Tooltip` with `permanent` prop is baked at creation time, so added `isActive` to the `CircleMarker` key to force remount
- Gap between main header and sticky trek header; set header to explicit `h-16` and matched with `top-16`

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Changed
- Complete homepage redesign for a more distinctive, less generic look
- Hero: split layout with floating image cards, gradient text, trust indicators, wave SVG transition
- Activities: bento grid with real photography and hover-reveal descriptions
- Featured treks: cards with glassmorphism price badges
- Testimonials: dark section with glassmorphism cards and glow effects on hover
- CTA: full-bleed background image with dual action buttons

### Added
- 28 real images sourced from Unsplash served locally (`public/images/`)
  - Trek hero images for all 6 treks
  - Activity category photos (hiking, yoga, temples, paragliding, rafting, skiing, city tours)
  - Gallery page photos
  - Hero banner, sidebar, and CTA background images
- Gallery page with masonry layout and lightbox (prev/next navigation, keyboard-friendly)

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect
- Language switcher in header (swaps `/en/...` <-> `/zh/...`)
- Nepal-inspired color theme: forest green, earth tone, adventure orange
- **Pages**: Home, About, Treks (listing + 6 detail pages), Team, Gallery, Contact
- **6 fully detailed treks** with bilingual content:
  - Everest Base Camp (14 days, challenging, $1,800)
  - Annapurna Circuit (18 days, challenging, $1,600)
  - Langtang Valley (10 days, moderate, $900)
  - Manaslu Circuit (16 days, strenuous, $2,200)
  - Poon Hill (5 days, easy, $500)
  - Upper Mustang (14 days, moderate, $2,500)
- Day-by-day itineraries with expandable accordion UI for each trek
- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

# Changelog

All notable changes to the Find Nepal Trek website are documented here.

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **Interactive trek route maps** on each trek detail page using Leaflet + react-leaflet
  - GPS coordinate data for all 6 treks (85 waypoints total)
  - Map stays zoomed out showing the full route; completed portion progressively highlights in orange as user scrolls
  - Day markers with tooltips — active day is enlarged with a permanent tooltip, completed markers filled orange, upcoming faded

- **Sticky trek header** (`StickyTrekHeader.tsx`) that slides in below the main nav after scrolling past the hero

- New files: `TrekMap.tsx`, `ItineraryWithMap.tsx`, `AltitudeProfile.tsx`, `StickyTrekHeader.tsx`, `trekCoordinates.ts`
- Dependencies: `leaflet`, `react-leaflet`, `@types/leaflet`

### Changed
- **About page content updated** to match original WordPress site copy
  - Hero title changed to "About Us" / "關於我們"
  - Story section uses authentic bilingual copy: "台灣女婿" / "台灣女兒" phrasing
  - All 6 principle titles and descriptions updated to match WordPress originals (more literary/poetic tone)
  - English translations rewritten to faithfully reflect the Chinese source
- **Team page updated**: 3 members (Shiva, guide2, Rainbow) with real photos where available

  - 3-column grid on desktop; gracefully handles empty name/role/bio/languages
- **About page principle cards redesigned**: removed generic Heroicon bubbles, replaced with numbered editorial layout (left accent border, large decorative `01`–`06` watermark numbers, rounded cards with shadow)
- Stats section (years experience, happy trekkers, etc.) commented out until real numbers confirmed
- Replaced all 6 trek hero images with higher-quality, trek-specific Unsplash photos
- Main header set to explicit `h-16` for consistent layout
- Disabled elastic/rubber-band overscroll globally (`overscroll-behavior: none`)
- **Contact page redesigned**: removed form, replaced with phone/WhatsApp card, email card with pre-filled mailto template, numbered checklist of what to include, and info cards (location, response time, languages)
- Removed Contact from header and footer navigation (still reachable via booking CTAs throughout the site)
- Trek detail page layout: replaced standalone itinerary accordion with side-by-side itinerary + map view

  - Gallery page photos

## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- Full bilingual site (English + Traditional Chinese) with 28 static pages
- i18n system using `[lang]` dynamic route segments with dictionary JSON files
- Client-side language detection via `navigator.language` with automatic redirect

- Team page with 4 member profiles
- Contact page with mailto-based form
- Responsive header with mobile hamburger menu
- Footer with sitemap links and social icons
- SEO metadata for all pages

### Technical
- Next.js 16 with App Router, static export (`output: "export"`)
- TypeScript strict mode, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4
- `images: { unoptimized: true }` for static export compatibility
- Inter font (Latin) + Noto Sans TC (Chinese) via Google Fonts `<link>` tag
- Custom CSS animations: fadeIn, fadeInUp, slideInFromLeft

### Added
- Initial Next.js project setup with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, App Router
- Static export configuration
- Private GitHub repository at `chiumax/find-nepal-trek-website`

message.content: this is what claude says when vfetching the site deployed on vercel Good question — the Vercel site is likely a **client-side rendered React/Next.js SPA** that requires JavaScript execution to render content. My fetch tool just grabs the raw HTML response, and all it gets back is:  ``` Find Nepal Trek | 發現尼泊爾 Loading... ```  That's the initial HTML shell before React hydrates and renders the actual UI. My fetcher doesn't run JavaScript, so it can't see the rendered content.  A few possible reasons specific to your build:  1. **No SSR/SSG configured** — If you're using Next.js with `'use client'` on everything or a pure React SPA (like Vite), there's no server-rendered HTML for crawlers to see 2. **Data fetching is all client-side** — If trek data, hero content, etc. loads via `useEffect` after mount, the initial response is empty 3. **This is also an SEO problem** — Google can execute JS but it's slower and less reliable. Googlebot may see the same empty shell, which means your trek pages might not get indexed well  This is actually worth flagging to your client — if the site isn't using SSR or static generation for key pages, it'll hurt their search rankings. For a trekking company that depends on organic search traffic, that's a big deal.  Are you using Next.js with App Router? If so, making the main pages server components (or using `generateStaticParams` for trek pages) would fix both the crawlability and the initial load time. https://find-nepal-trek-website.vercel.app/

Everest Base Camp Trek

The Everest Base Camp trek is the ultimate Himalayan adventure, tracing the footsteps of legendary mountaineers Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay into the heart of the Khumbu region. Beginning with a dramatic flight to Lukla and winding through ancient Sherpa villages, rhododendron forests, and glacial moraines, this iconic route delivers an unparalleled sense of scale as you approach the world's highest peak. Along the way you'll cross suspension bridges draped with prayer flags, visit the historic Tengboche Monastery framed by Ama Dablam, and witness yak caravans carrying supplies to high-altitude camps. The trek reaches its climax at Everest Base Camp (5,364 m), where the Khumbu Icefall groans and shifts beneath the South Col route used by summit expeditions. An early-morning ascent of Kala Patthar (5,545 m) rewards you with a panoramic sunrise over Everest, Lhotse, and Nuptse that few experiences on Earth can rival. Throughout the journey, the warmth of Sherpa hospitality in cosy teahouses makes the high-altitude nights memorable for more than just the star-filled skies. This is a trek that demands respect — proper acclimatisation days are built into the itinerary, and our experienced guides monitor your health at every stage. Whether you are a seasoned trekker ticking off a bucket-list goal or an adventurous traveller seeking a life-changing challenge, the Everest Base Camp trek delivers memories that will stay with you forever.

14 days5,364m
View Details
Challenging
From $1600

Annapurna Circuit Trek

The Annapurna Circuit is widely regarded as one of the greatest long-distance treks on the planet. Circumnavigating the entire Annapurna massif, this epic route traverses an extraordinary range of landscapes — from subtropical rice paddies and bamboo forests in the lowlands to arid, Tibetan-influenced high desert beyond Manang. The cultural tapestry is equally rich, as you pass through Hindu villages, Gurung settlements, and Tibetan Buddhist communities, each with their own distinct architecture, festivals, and cuisine. The centrepiece of the trek is the crossing of Thorong La Pass (5,416 m), one of the highest trekking passes in the world. The pre-dawn ascent is gruelling but the reward at the top — prayer flags snapping in the wind against a backdrop of snow-capped giants — is a moment of pure exhilaration. The descent into the sacred temple town of Muktinath, a pilgrimage site for both Hindus and Buddhists, provides a fitting spiritual counterpoint to the physical achievement. With its incredible diversity of ecosystems, cultures, and terrain, the Annapurna Circuit offers a complete Himalayan experience in a single trek. Well-maintained teahouse networks mean you can travel with a lighter pack, and the gradual altitude gain on the eastern approach provides excellent natural acclimatisation. This is a trek for those who want depth, variety, and a genuine sense of journey.

18 days5,416m
View Details
Moderate
From $900

Langtang Valley Trek

The Langtang Valley trek offers an intimate Himalayan experience without the crowds found on Nepal's most famous routes. Located just north of Kathmandu, this beautiful valley was once described by the first Briton to visit it, Bill Tilman, as "one of the most beautiful valleys in the world." The trail follows the Langtang Khola through dense forests of oak, maple, and rhododendron, alive with birdlife and the occasional red panda sighting, before opening into wide alpine meadows surrounded by a spectacular ring of snow-capped peaks. The highlight of the trek is the journey to Kyanjin Gompa (3,870 m), a small Buddhist monastery and cheese factory nestled beneath the massive Langtang Lirung (7,227 m). From here, a day hike to Tserko Ri (4,984 m) offers one of the finest viewpoints in the Nepal Himalaya, with a 360-degree panorama that includes Langtang Lirung, Dorje Lakpa, Ganesh Himal, and on clear days the distant profile of Shishapangma in Tibet. The Langtang region was devastated by the 2015 earthquake, and the rebuilt village stands as a testament to the resilience of the Tamang people. Trekking here directly supports the local communities in their recovery. With its accessibility from Kathmandu, moderate altitude, and rich cultural heritage, the Langtang Valley trek is an ideal choice for those seeking an authentic, less-commercialised Himalayan adventure.

我已經為您搜尋了台灣網頁設計報價和費用的相關資訊。以下是2025年台灣形象網站設計的主要費用資訊：

## 形象網站建置費用

形象網站的建置費用約在 NT$45,000～NT$70,000。根據不同的設計方式，費用範圍有所不同：

- **套版型網站**：費用約在$20,000～$50,000
- **半客製化網站**：價格落在$45,000～$60,000
- **全客製化官網**：費用則是$100,000起跳

## 其他網站類型費用參考

- 購物網站大約落在 NT$75,000～NT$120,000
- 客製化網站（例如具有特殊功能、整合系統），費用則可能從 NT$150,000 起跳

## 年度維護與額外費用

網站主機每年約需 NT$5,000～NT$12,000，網址費用每年 NT$700～NT$1,000 不等。網站維護費（年費或月費，約佔專案費用的 10～30%）

影響費用的主要因素包括網站複雜度、功能需求、設計深度、以及服務廠商的專業程度和經驗。建議在正式合作前詳細了解自身需求，以便獲得更準確的報價。

Here's how I'd think about pricing this project, given what was built and the local market context:

## What Was Built

- Custom Next.js 16 static site (not a WordPress template)
- Bilingual EN/ZH with full i18n system
- 6 detailed trek pages with day-by-day itineraries
- Interactive Leaflet maps with scroll-synced route progression + altitude profiles
- Responsive design, custom color scheme from logo, SEO/OG optimization
- ~30+ static pages total across both languages

## Market Comparisons

### Taiwan (台灣)
Taiwanese agencies typically quote:
- **Template sites (套版)**: NT$20,000–50,000 (~$600–1,500 USD)
- **Semi-custom (半客製)**: NT$45,000–60,000 (~$1,400–1,800 USD)
- **Fully custom (全客製)**: NT$100,000+ (~$3,000+ USD)

This project falls squarely in the **fully custom** category — bilingual, interactive maps, custom components, no CMS dependency. A Taiwan agency would likely quote **NT$80,000–150,000 ($2,500–4,700 USD)** for this scope.

### Nepal
Nepali agencies typically quote:
- **Basic sites**: NPR 60,000–180,000 (~$450–1,350 USD)
- **Complex/custom sites**: NPR 200,000–600,000+ (~$1,500–4,500 USD)

A Nepal agency would probably quote **NPR 250,000–500,000 ($1,900–3,800 USD)** for equivalent work.

## My Suggested Pricing

Given the bilingual niche (which straddles both markets) and the actual scope:

| Approach | Range |
|----------|-------|
| Budget-friendly (Nepal-market rate) | **$1,500–2,500** |
| Mid-market (Taiwan agency equivalent) | **$3,000–4,500** |
| Premium (reflecting interactive maps, i18n, SEO) | **$5,000–7,000** |

The interactive maps + altitude charts, bilingual content system, and SEO groundwork push this well beyond a "basic corporate site." If billing a Taiwan-based client, **$3,000–5,000 USD** feels fair. If the client is Nepal-based, **$2,000–3,000** is more realistic for the local market.

Sources:
- [Website Development Cost in Nepal (2025)](https://abstractinfosys.com/resource/website-development-cost-in-nepal)
- [Nepal Web Design Pricing - WebHouse Nepal](https://webhousenepal.com/blogs/website-design-and-development-price-in-nepal)
- [台灣網頁設計費用行情 - PRO360](https://www.pro360.com.tw/price/website_production)
- [2025 網站設計報價費用一覽 - Tasker](https://www.tasker.com.tw/articles/detail/1374)
